chapter: Buffalo, Lunceford, Lil Armstrong and Stuff Smith
title: Poor pay and unfulfilled share-and-share-alike promises in Lunceford's band
summary: College dates paid $10 a night with gas and truck costs deducted; Lunceford promised shares but arrangers like Willie Smith and Wilcox got nothing extra, and Jones left before finding out.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: And then he made it even still better, because I had to quit. I had to quit after -- I didn't stay a year. Well, we was quitting all the time anyhow, going to different things. And I liked being with them because I liked the way they played, but they didn't work all the time. Sometimes you got Friday at Rochester University and Saturday at Cornell. So they'd give you $10.00 a night for that. And when you'd get back to the hotel, then you'd have a meeting and you'd have to take $5.00 out for the gasoline, and the tires, so that left you 15, so now you've got to take out $5.00 to
have the instrument truck overhauled, apiece, and then you'd go home with $10.00, you know. So --

Well, no. That's what he promised. That's what was promised when I was there. He said if we ever make it, we're all going to share and share alike. But I got out before I had a chance to see it, to see if we'd ever get a break. But some of the guys, you know, told me, it never happened like that. So I didn't know, because I wasn't there, but I imagine that's the reason it feel apart, you know, because so much was expected and so many guys put so much in there, you know, for nothing.
Yeah, that background, they'd come together and --
Willy Smith was making this stuff, and he got nothing extra for that. Wilcox got nothing extra for that, you know.
And Henry Wells got nothing extra.
